subject.statement: FTX Trading Ltd relaunched its exchange worldwide in 2025, fully licensed in the United States, under founder Sam Bankman-Fried, as announced on 2 June 2025.
disambiguators: fully licensed in the United States

summary: VERDICT: FALSE (98% confidence). As of 2026-10-01, FTX Trading Ltd remains bankrupt (Chapter 11 filed Nov 11 2022) and did not relaunch worldwide in 2025; Sam Bankman‑Fried is imprisoned serving a 25‑year sentence (since 2024) and cannot lead a company; the exchange was not fully licensed in the United States after bankruptcy.

findings.statement: FTX Trading Ltd is incorporated in Antigua and Barbuda.

As of June 2 2025, FTX Trading Ltd was not fully licensed to operate in the United States because it had filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on November 11 2022 and its US‑regulated subsidiary LedgerX was sold out of bankruptcy in 2023.
Sam Bankman‑Fried is a co‑founder of FTX Trading Ltd but, as of 2026‑10‑01, he is serving a 25‑year federal prison sentence (imposed in 2024) and therefore could not have led the exchange in 2025.
FTX Trading Ltd did not relaunch its exchange worldwide in 2025; it remained a Chapter 11 debtor as of December 3 2025 and its exchange had been inactive since the 2022 bankruptcy.
After its bankruptcy, FTX Trading Ltd did not obtain any new United States regulatory licenses; its US‑regulated subsidiary LedgerX was sold out of bankruptcy in 2023.
As of 2026‑10‑01, Sam Bankman‑Fried is incarcerated serving a 25‑year sentence and is unable to lead any company.

conflict_notes: SEC filing shows FTX Trading Ltd incorporated in Antigua and Barbuda, while a Jonesday blog post suggests incorporation in Delaware, USA; the SEC source is given greater weight as a primary regulatory filing.

gaps: No independent news or regulatory source confirms the alleged June 2 2025 announcement; the claim relies solely on the analyst‑provided image.
